notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped.
No resistor is used: the button is wired between pin 2 and GND and relies on the internal INPUT_PULLUP.

From the image, the button straddles the centre gap in breadboard columns 24 and 25. Side 1 (1.l, 1.r) is in column 24 and side 2 (2.l, 2.r) is in column 25. Pressing the button joins the two columns.
The black wire goes from the Uno GND header pin (next to AREF) to hole 24t.a. The yellow wire goes from Uno pin 2 to hole 25t.a.
The Uno has several GND pins and the image shows the one on the digital header next to AREF. I assumed that is GND.1.
The breadboard hole names map the image's numbered rows to column numbers and its letters to row letters, in the catalogue's '<column><bank>.<row>' scheme.
